'''Hinduja Group''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]], based in [[Mumbai]]. The group is present in eleven sectors including [[automotive]], [[oil]] and [[speciality chemicals]], [[banking]] and [[finance]], IT and ITeS, [[cyber security]], [[healthcare]], [[trading]], [[infrastructure]] project development, [[Media (communication)|media]] and [[entertainment]], power, and [[real estate]]. The net worth of the Hinduja brothers was estimated to be {{USD|32}} billion in 2022, making them the wealthiest people in the United Kingdom.<ref name="srigopi">{{Cite news |title=Sri and Gopi Hinduja net worth — Sunday Times Rich List 2022 |newspaper=[[The Times]] |language=en |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sunday-times-rich-list/profile/article/gopi-hinduja-and-family-net-worth-sunday-times-rich-list-5m5r8xfgh |access-date=2022-10-04 |issn=0140-0460}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The Sunday Times Rich List 2022|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sunday-times-rich-list |access-date=2023-05-17|website=The Times}}</ref> 

In October 2024, the Hinduja family was ranked 11th on the Forbes list of India’s 100 richest tycoons, with a net worth of $22 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2024 |title=India's 100 Richest |url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/india-billionaires/ |website=India’s 100 Richest}}</ref> In May 2025, as per the ''[[The Sunday Times|Sunday Times]]'' rich list, the Hinduja family topped UK's richest list for the fourth consecutive year, with a net worth of £35.3 billion.<ref name="srigopi"/><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/uk/hinduja-family-tops-uks-sunday-times-rich-list-for-fourth-year-check-out-the-full-list-of-billionaires/articleshow/121266872.cms | title=Hinduja family tops UK's Sunday Times Rich List for fourth year; check out the full list of billionaires | website=timesofindia.indiatimes.com}}</ref> In 2026, according to the Sunday Times Rich List, the Hinduja family became the UK's richest for the fifth consecutive term, with a net worth of £38 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Sunday Times Rich List 2026 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sunday-times-rich-list |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rich List 2026: Hindujas crowned Britain's richest family with a $43 billion fortune—5th year in a row |url=https://www.firstpost.com/business/rich-list-2026-hindujas-crowned-britains-richest-family-with-a-43-billion-fortune-5th-year-in-a-row-14011581.html}}</ref>

==History==
The company was founded in 1914 by [[Parmanand Hinduja]], who was from a [[Sindhis|Sindhi]] family based in India.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/hinduja-a-relatively-successful-billionaire-1.492214/|title=Hinduja, a 'relatively' successful billionaire|work=The National|date=24 December 2010|access-date=5 August 2016|first=Farah|last=Halime|quote=The family's success began with their father, Parmanand, who came from the Sindh province of what is now Pakistan...}}</ref> Initially operating in [[Shikarpur, Sindh|Shikarpur]] (in modern-day [[Pakistan]]) and [[Bombay]], India, he set up the company's first international operation in Iran in 1919. The headquarters of the group remained in [[Iran]] until 1979, when the [[Islamic Revolution]] forced it to move to [[Europe]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Podcast {{!}} The business of family — The Hindujas|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/podcast-the-business-of-family-the-hindujas-2732971.html|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Moneycontrol|date=19 July 2018 }}</ref><ref name="bloomberg">{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Hugo |first2=Jonathan |last2=Browning |title=Billionaire Family Feud Puts a Century-Old Business Empire in Jeopardy |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2021-11-24/billionaire-family-feud-puts-a-century-old-business-empire-in-jeopardy |access-date=28 November 2021 |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=23 November 2021}}</ref>

Group Chairman [[S. P. Hinduja|Srichand Hinduja]] and his brother [[Gopichand Hinduja|Gopichand]], also Co-Chairman, moved to [[London]] in 1979 to develop the export business; the third brother [[Prakash Hinduja|Prakash]] manages the group's operations in [[Geneva]], Switzerland while the youngest brother, Ashok, oversees the Indian interests.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/this-is-dynasty-indianstyle-1323548.html|title=This is Dynasty, Indian-style|author=Tim McGirk|date=12 January 1996|work=The Independent}}</ref>

The group employs over 200,000 people and has offices in many major cities around the world including in India.<ref name=company/> In 2017, Srichand and Gopichand Hinduja were described as the wealthiest men in [[United Kingdom|Britain]] with an estimated wealth of {{currency|16.2|GBP}} billion in the [[Sunday Times Rich List 2017|''Sunday Times'' Rich List 2017]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/hinduja-brothers-stay-on-top-of-uk-rich-list/story-MEX4oShlu1WdNS7uElnzNP.html| title = Hinduja brothers stay on top of UK rich list| author = Sonwalkar, Prasun| date = 7 May 2017| access-date = 7 May 2017| publisher = Hindusthan Times}}</ref>

==Controversies==

===Bofors scandal===
{{Main|Bofors scandal}}
Srichand, Gopichand and Prakash Hinduja were connected with the investigation into the [[Bofors scandal]], in which Swedish firm [[Bofors]] was alleged to have paid illegal bribes to government officials and politicians in connection with the {{USD}}1.3 billion sale of 400 [[howitzers]] to the Indian Government in 1986. The three brothers were charged by the Indian [[Central Bureau of Investigation]] in October 2000,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/south_asia/964191.stm|title=BBC News - SOUTH ASIA - Bofors charges against Hindujas}}</ref> but in 2005 the High Court in Delhi threw out all charges against them, citing a lack of evidence and saying that documents central to the prosecution case were "useless and dubious" since their provenance could not be verified. Judge RS Sodhi said: "I must express my disapproval that 14 years of trial and {{INRConvert|2.5|b}} of public money was spent on the case. It has caused huge economical, emotional, professional and personal loss to the Hindujas."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/2474787.stm|title=BBC NEWS - South Asia - Q&A: Hinduja Bofors case|date=31 May 2005}}</ref>

===2001 Hinduja affair===
In January 2001, it was revealed that UK government Minister [[Peter Mandelson]] had telephoned [[Home Office]] minister [[Mike O'Brien (UK politician)|Mike O'Brien]] on behalf of Srichand Hinduja, who was at the time seeking British citizenship, and whose family firm was to become the main sponsor of the "Faith Zone" in the [[Millennium Dome]]. Consequently, on 24 January 2001 Mandelson resigned from the Government for a second time,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/1134819.stm |title=BBC News | SOUTH ASIA | Mandelson resigns over Hinduja affair |publisher=News.bbc.co.uk |date= 24 January 2001<!--, 14:30 GMT -->|access-date=3 October 2008}}</ref><ref>{{London Gazette|issue=56106 |page=1223|date=31 January 2001
}}</ref> insisting he had done nothing wrong. An independent enquiry by Sir Anthony Hammond came to the conclusion that neither Mandelson nor anyone else had acted improperly.

In January 2001, immigration minister [[Barbara Roche]] revealed in a written Commons reply that [[Keith Vaz]], [[Member of Parliament]] for [[Leicester East (UK Parliament constituency)|Leicester East]] and at the time a [[Foreign Office]] minister, and other MPs, had also contacted the [[Home Office]] about the Hinduja brothers, saying that Vaz had made inquiries about when a decision on their application for citizenship could be expected.<ref>{{cite news | last = Grice | first = Andrew | title = MPs to quiz Mandelson on passport for Hinduja | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 22 January 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/mps-to-quiz-mandelson-on-passport-for-hinduja-702939.html | location=London}}</ref>

On 25 January, Vaz became the focus of Opposition questions about the Hinduja affair and many parliamentary questions were tabled, demanding that he fully disclose his role. Vaz said via a [[Foreign Office]] spokesman that he would be "fully prepared" to answer questions put to him by Sir Anthony Hammond QC who had been asked by the Prime Minister to carry out an inquiry into the affair. Vaz said that he had known the Hinduja brothers for some time; he had been present when the charitable Hinduja Foundation was set up in 1993, and had also delivered a speech in 1998 when the brothers invited Tony and [[Cherie Blair]] to a [[Diwali]] celebration.<ref>{{cite news | last = Sengupta| first = Kim | title = Vaz sidesteps questions on links with Hindujas | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 26 January 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/vaz-sidesteps-questions-on-links-with-hindujas-704370.html | location=London}}</ref>

On 26 January 2001, [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Tony Blair]] was accused of prejudicing the independent inquiry into the Hinduja passport affair, after he declared that Keith Vaz had not done "anything wrong". On the same day, Vaz told reporters that they would "regret" their behaviour once the facts of the case were revealed. "Some of you are going to look very foolish when this report comes out. Some of the stuff you said about Peter, and about others and me, you'll regret very much when the facts come out," he said. When asked why the passport application of one of the Hinduja brothers had been processed more quickly than normal, being processed and sanctioned in six months when the process can take up to two years, he replied, "It is not unusual."<ref>{{cite news | last = Waugh | first = Paul |author2=Kim Sengupta | title = Vaz defiant over his role in Hinduja passport scandal | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 27 January 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/vaz-defiant-over-his-role-in-hinduja-passport-scandal-704469.html | location=London}}</ref>

On 29 January, the government confirmed that the Hinduja Foundation had held a reception for Vaz in September 1999 to celebrate his appointment as the first Asian Minister in recent times. The party was not listed by Vaz in the House of Commons Register of Members' Interests and [[John Redwood]], then head of the Conservative Parliamentary Campaigns Unit, questioned Vaz's judgement in accepting the hospitality.<ref>{{cite news | last = Woolf | first = Marie | title = Hindujas held party to celebrate Vaz being appointed a minister | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 30 January 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/hindujas-held-party-to-celebrate-vaz-being-appointed-a-minister-704847.html | location=London}}</ref>

In March, Vaz was ordered to fully co-operate with a new inquiry launched into his financial affairs by [[Elizabeth Filkin]], who was [[Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards]] at the time. [[Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs|Foreign Secretary]] [[Robin Cook]], Vaz's superior, also urged him to fully answer allegations about his links with the Hinduja brothers. Mr Vaz met Mrs Filkin on 20 March to discuss a complaint that the Hinduja Foundation had given the sum of £1,200 to Mapesbury Communications, a company run by his wife, in return for helping to organise a Hinduja-sponsored reception at the House of Commons. Vaz had previously denied receiving money from the Hindujas, but insisted that he made no personal gain from the transaction in question.<ref>{{cite news | last = Woolf| first = Marie | title = Filkin launches new investigation into cash links between Vaz and Hindujas | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 22 March 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/filkin-launches-new-investigation-into-cash-links-between-vaz-and-hindujas-688445.html | location=London}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | last = Grice | first = Andrew |author2=Stephen Castle | title = Downing Street orders Vaz to help inquiry | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 24 March 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/downing-street-orders-vaz-to-help-inquiry-688728.html | location=London}}</ref>

In June 2001, Vaz admitted that he had made representations during the [[Hinduja brothers]]' applications for British citizenship while a backbench MP. Tony Blair also admitted that Vaz had "made representations" on behalf of other Asians.<ref>{{Citation | last1 = George | first1 = Jones | last2 = Womack | first2 = Sarah | title = Vaz admits greater role over Hinduja passport | newspaper = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | date = 19 June 2001 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1319668/Vaz-admits-greater-role-over-Hinduja-passport.html | location=London}}</ref> On 11 June 2001 Vaz was dismissed from his post as Europe Minister, to be replaced by [[Peter Hain]]. The Prime Minister's office said that Vaz had written to Tony Blair stating he wished to stand down for health reasons.<ref>{{cite news | last = Woolf | first = Marie |author2=Andrew Morris | title = After months of claims and counter claims, Vaz is finally sacked as Minister for Europe | work = [[The Independent]] | date = 12 June 2001 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/after-months-of-claims-and-counter-claims-vaz-is-finally-sacked-as-minister-for-europe-673703.html | location=London}}</ref>

In December 2001, Elizabeth Filkin cleared Vaz of failing to register payments to his wife's law firm by the Hinduja brothers, but said that he had colluded with his wife to conceal the payments. Filkin's report said that the payments had been given to his wife for legal advice on immigration issues and concluded that Vaz had gained no direct personal benefit, and that Commons rules did not require him to disclose payments made to his wife. She did, however, criticise him for his secrecy, saying, "It is clear to me there has been deliberate collusion over many months between Mr Vaz and his wife to conceal this fact and to prevent me from obtaining accurate information about his possible financial relationship with the Hinduja family".<ref>{{cite news | last = Wintour | first = Patrick | title = Vaz cleared over Hinduja payments to wife | work = [[The Guardian]] | date = 24 December 2001 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2001/dec/24/houseofcommons.labour | location=London}}</ref>

===Ashok Leyland===
In February 2005, [[Ashok Leyland]], a company within the Hinduja Group, announced an agreement to supply 100 army vehicles to the [[Sudan]]ese Defence Ministry. It included the sale of 20 Ashok Leyland "Stallion" 4x4 military trucks, valued at $750,000. Initially, it was alleged to be used to transport or carry weapons, but it was later found to be intended for humanitarian purposes. Since then, the organisation has not engaged in Sudan's defence sales.

===Human trafficking trial===
In June 2024, a [[human trafficking]] trial began in Switzerland against four members of the Hinduja family, who were accused of [[Exploitation of labour|exploiting]] household staff at their lakeside villa in [[Geneva]], by reportedly paying as little as $8 for workdays lasting 15 to 18 hours and confiscating their passports. The allegations were refuted by a lawyer representing the family. It was also claimed that the family spent more on pets than they paid a servant.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Roeloffs |first=Mary Whitfill |title=Billionaire Hinduja Family Accused Of Confiscating Staff Passports, Forcing 18-Hour Work Days |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2024/06/17/billionaire-hinduja-family-accused-of-confiscating-staff-passports-forcing-18-hour-work-days/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> The Swiss court dismissed the human trafficking charges, but found them guilty of exploiting the staff; it sentenced [[Prakash Hinduja]], wife Kamal, son Ajay and daughter-in-law Namrata to four and a half years of imprisonment.<ref>{{cite news |title=Swiss court sentences Prakash Hinduja, 3 family members to 4.5 years in jail |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/swiss-court-sentences-prakash-hinduja-3-family-members-to-4-1-2-years-in-jail-101718986311844.html |access-date=21 June 2024 |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

Hinduja Group is an Indian multinational conglomerate, based in Mumbai. The group is present in eleven sectors including automotive, oil and speciality chemicals, banking and finance, IT and ITeS, cyber security, healthcare, trading, infrastructure project development, media and entertainment, power, and real estate. The net worth of the Hinduja brothers was estimated to be US$32 billion in 2022, making them the wealthiest people in the United Kingdom. 
In October 2024, the Hinduja family was ranked 11th on the Forbes list of India’s 100 richest tycoons, with a net worth of $22 billion. In May 2025, as per the Sunday Times rich list, the Hinduja family topped UK's richest list for the fourth consecutive year, with a net worth of £35.3 billion. In 2026, according to the Sunday Times Rich List, the Hinduja family became the UK's richest for the fifth consecutive term, with a net worth of £38 billion.
